card.summary: Yes. You can use it for free. However, in the case of free users, there are restrictions on usage time, transmission speed, and amount of transmission data.

free_tier.stated: Yes. You can use it for free. However, in the case of free users, there are restrictions on usage time, transmission speed, and amount of transmission data.

egress.terms: The vendor states restrictions on usage time, transmission speed, and amount of transmission data, with no numbers published. The support forum answers the same question with: At this moment, no restriction because it is under alpha status.; ingress: tcp+udp

record.tooling: Single binary from mudcat.io/download, subcommands tcp, http and udp.
record.chaining: Carries a WireGuard handshake to a free VM, or exposes a game server directly; the 8-hour hostname means it needs a supervisor that re-registers and re-points DNS.

limits.value: Access Domain TTL: valid for 8.00 hours for TCP and UDP tunnels
unpublished restriction on amount of transmission data

record.binding_note: Free tier port lease expires after 8 hours. Data volume policies are unstated in published terms.

identity_cost.detail: The client assigns a Device UUID and needs no account, email or card on the page read; the download page lists only operating-system binaries.

record.reliability_note: Alpha software at version 0.0.3; hostnames expire every 8 hours; the vendor reserves the right to cap time, speed and data without publishing numbers.
record.confidence_note: The free-tier byte and speed limits are unpublished; one measured transfer and a reconnect after 8 hours would move this from documented to measured.

evidence.proved: HTTP, TCP and UDP port sharing; UDP example with an 8-hour Access Domain TTL; free use with unpublished restrictions on time, speed and data.
Vendor staff answer of 2024-08-13 that there is no restriction while the service is in alpha, which means the published restriction has no number behind it.
Client version 0.0.3 for Windows, macOS and Linux, which supports the alpha reading.
'Yes, it can be used free of charge. However, in the case of free users there are restrictions on usage time, transmission speed, amount of transmitted data and so on'; no figure is published

record.notes: The alpha status is the important fact: the free tier works today with no stated cap, and the caps are promised but unwritten. Version 0.0.3 and a 2024 forum thread mean this is not a 2026 launch, only a 2026-live one. The conservative verdict is kept: the 8-hour lease and an unpublished byte cap both defeat the test, and neither can be designed against.

extras.wg_detail: The vendor documents a UDP forwarding mode: Forwarding: UDP 583-841-3346.mudcat.io:25566 -> 127.0.0.1:25565. A WireGuard handshake is an opaque UDP datagram and passes through that path.
extras.volume_stated: The vendor states restrictions on usage time, transmission speed, and amount of transmission data, with no numbers published. The support forum answers the same question with: At this moment, no restriction because it is under alpha status.
extras.transit_note: A Mudfish-operated remote access node forwards the datagrams.
